## 1. New LLM Versions / Major AI Lab Tools

**Meta Brain2Qwerty v2**
- **Date:** 2026-06-29
- **Primary source:** [Meta AI — Brain2Qwerty](https://ai.meta.com/blog/brain2qwerty-brain-ai-human-communication/)
- **Summary:** Meta released Brain2Qwerty v2, associated code, and research on non-invasive brain-to-text decoding from MEG recordings. Meta reports average word accuracy of 61%, with 78% for the best participant, using end-to-end deep learning and LLM fine-tuning to decode typed natural sentences.
- **Why it matters:** This is a meaningful lab-tool/research advance in AI-mediated human-computer interaction. It remains experimental and hardware-constrained, but the reported accuracy moves non-invasive neural text decoding closer to practical assistive communication research.

## 2. FOSS / Open-Weight LMs & Tools

**Chinese open-weight cyber AI capability lead**
- **Date:** 2026-06-29
- **Source:** [Wall Street Journal — China Has Matched Anthropic in Cybersecurity, Resetting AI Race](https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/chinese-ai-anthropic-mythos-cybersecurity-574b02c2)
- **Summary:** WSJ reported that Z.ai’s open-weight GLM-5.2 and 360 Security’s Tulongfeng tool have narrowed the gap with leading U.S. cyber-focused AI systems in bug-finding scenarios. This is retained as a single-source lead.
- **Why it matters:** If validated, open-weight cyber-capable models would broaden defensive access while increasing misuse risk. Do not treat the benchmark claim as confirmed without primary evaluations or independent replication.
